checks.title: Headline vs per-attack-type results
checks.summary: Overall 97.4% caught at 0.130% false alarms. Weak types hidden by the average: Botnet, Portscan.
details: overall: 97.4% of attacks caught, 0.130% of normal traffic flagged (354 false alarms)
largest attack type: DDoS = 98% of all attack flows
checks.rule: FAIL if under 50% of attacks are caught; WARN if one type is over half of all attacks or any type with 30+ examples is under 50%

checks.title: False alarms as alerts per hour
checks.summary: 44.2 false alerts per hour over 8.0 hours; 99.6% of all alerts are real attacks.
details: an analyst can typically review tens of alerts per hour, not thousands
checks.rule: PASS up to 10 per hour, WARN up to 100, FAIL above; depends on team size

checks.title: Seen vs unseen attack types
checks.summary: Unseen types: 97.4% caught (97,563 flows). Seen types: n/a (0 flows).
details: unseen types in this data: Botnet, DDoS, Portscan
every attack type here is unseen, so this is a genuine zero-day test; there is nothing seen to compare against
checks.rule: WARN if unseen types are caught 20+ points less often than seen ones

checks.title: Classifier veto of detector alarms
checks.summary: Of 96,823 attacks the detector caught, the final output called 1.8% normal. Worst: Botnet, 100.0% of its detector catches overruled.
checks.rule: WARN if more than 20% of the detector's correct alarms are overruled, overall or for any type with 30+ catches

checks.title: Ranking quality without a threshold (AUROC)
checks.summary: AUROC 0.908 (0.5 = chance, 1.0 = perfect ranking). Weak types: Botnet 0.55.
checks.rule: PASS at 0.9+ with every type (30+ examples) at 0.7+; WARN at 0.7-0.9 or if any type is below 0.7; FAIL below 0.7 overall

checks.title: Identical rows in training and test data
checks.summary: 0.32% of test rows also appear exactly in the training data (82 feature columns compared).
details: attack rows that also appear in training: 0.00% of 97,563
normal rows that also appear in training: 0.43% of 272,696 (short, common normal flows repeat naturally)
identical attack rows let a model memorise answers instead of learning patterns
checks.rule: WARN above 1% overall, or above 1% of attack rows

checks.title: Can these stage sequences test forecasting?
checks.summary: 5 real stage changes in 1 episodes; the one-line rule 'advance one stage' gets 1/5 (20%, 95% CI 1%-72%); best possible for any rule using the current stage: 80%.
details: uncertainty about the next stage: 0.400 bits (0 = fully predictable)
checks.rule: FAIL if the trivial rule already reaches the ceiling, or there are fewer than 30 stage changes: no forecaster can then show an advantage
